problems.title: 1. The Bear. · Groups α β
problems.statement:
The White Bear (whom was already met in the texts of the VII, VIII and IX International Astronomy Olympiads) has returned from Crimea to the North Pole and decided to observe a sunset. Calculate how long this sunset lasts. The solution has to include a picture with an image of the Bear on the North Pole; necessary sizes or angular sizes should be in the picture. Assume that the Earth is spherical. Recollect for yourself the necessary information about the White Bear.

But can the Bear prolong the observation of sunset, not moving from the Pole? For what time?

difficulty.rationale: Combine annual solar motion, obliquity and horizon depression.

provenance.evidence: Complete personal visual reading of native question page 1 and native theory-sketch pages 4; estimated relative to stated prerequisites, no human calibration and no separate model checker.

solution.statement:
For an observer on the North Pole the sunset happens once a year, in time close to the day of the autumnal equinox. For the observer on the North Pole the angle between the ecliptic and the horizon is equal to $\varepsilon=23.5^{\circ}$. During the sunset the Sun lowers to the angle equal to its apparent angular diameter, that is $\alpha=32'$. During this time the Sun transits angular distance on ecliptic is equal to $\varphi=\alpha/\sin\varepsilon$. Thus, the duration of sunset is $\tau=\varphi/v=\alpha/(v\cdot\sin\varepsilon)$, where $v$ is the speed of the Sun on the ecliptic, equal to $v=360^{\circ}/365.25^{\mathrm d}=0.986^{\circ}$ per day. Thus,

$$\tau=(32/60)^{\circ}/(360^{\circ}/365.25^{\mathrm d})/\sin23.5^{\circ}=1.36\ \text{days or}\ 32.5\ \text{hours}.$$

Yes, during the sunset the Bear will come to twist the head 490 degrees!

As for the prolongation of the observation of the sunset, the Bear can use the effect of depression of the physical horizon, if it rises on the back feet. That is, he can begin to observe sunset lying on ground (pardon, on ice), where the horizon dip can be disregarded, and to finish, costing on back feet. For the last case the depression of the physical horizon makes

$$\Delta\varphi=\arccos(R/(R+h))\approx((R+h)^2-R^2)^{1/2}/R\approx(2h/R)^{1/2}\quad\text{(in radians)}.$$

Where $R$ is the radius of the Earth, and $h$ is the height of eye level above the surface of the Earth (ice). For the height of an eye of a White Bear about 2 m above the surface, the horizon depression is about $3'$. So, the Bear can prolong observation of sunset almost by 10 %, namely,

$$\Delta\tau=(3/60)^{\circ}/(360^{\circ}/365.25^{\mathrm d})/\sin23.5^{\circ}\approx3\ \text{hours}.$$

problems.title: 2. Sun. · Groups α β
problems.statement:
In one of the ancient models of the Universe the centre of solar system is the Earth rotating around its own axis. The stars are not moving around the Earth. The Moon and the Sun are orbiting the Earth. Mercury and Venus are orbiting the Sun. Mars, Jupiter and Saturn moves around invisible objects which are orbiting the Earth.

Consider the explanation of the system Earth-Moon to be correct in this model and the mass of Sun to be negligible in comparison with the mass of the Earth-Moon system and find (by two different ways of solution) the distance between the Earth and the Sun in such a model.

Find the absolute stellar magnitude of such a Sun.

difficulty.rationale: Compare two hypothetical Kepler systems and connect distance to magnitude; the native sketch is partial.

provenance.evidence: Complete personal visual reading of native question page 1 and native theory-sketch pages 4; estimated relative to stated prerequisites, no human calibration and no separate model checker.

solution.statement: The both ways are to use the III General Kepler's law. The first way is to compare the system Earth-SunInModel (365.25 days) with system Earth-Moon (27.37 days) taking into account the same total mass of system. The second way is to compare the system Earth-SunInModel (total mass of system is mass of Earth+Moon) with real system Earth-Sun (total mass of system is mass of Sun+Earth+Moon ≈ mass of Sun).
solution.incompleteReason: The native sketch supplies only the two Kepler-law comparisons. It prints no calculated distance or absolute stellar magnitude, so no missing numerical results are invented.

problems.title: 3. Andromeda nebula. · Groups α β
problems.statement: We hope that you are familiar with the object of Andromeda nebula (M31, NGC 224). Its stellar magnitude is $m=4.4^{\mathrm m}$ and its distance from us is $0.7\ \mathrm{Mpc}$. To what distance from this object should we move, if it were to shine as the full Moon? What would the (approximate) angular size of this object be in that case?

answer.note: The native sketch prints N = exp(17.1/5) = 2630; that printed expression is retained without scientific correction.

difficulty.rationale: Magnitude scaling must be assessed against the galaxy’s extended physical size.

provenance.evidence: Complete personal visual reading of native question page 1 and native theory-sketch pages 4; estimated relative to stated prerequisites, no human calibration and no separate model checker.

solution.statement:
The full Moon stellar magnitude is $m_M=-12.7^{\mathrm m}$. So we should come nearer to the Andromeda nebula so that the stellar magnitude changes from $m=4.4^{\mathrm m}$ to $m_M=-12.7^{\mathrm m}$, i.e. for $\Delta m=17.1^{\mathrm m}$. The formal calculation gives us $N=\exp(17.1/5)=2630$ times. $0.7\ \mathrm{Mpc}/2630\approx270\ \mathrm{pc}$. Taking into account that the angular size of the Andromeda nebula in our sky is about $2^{\circ}$–$3^{\circ}$, i.e. the linear size is about $5\cdot10^{-2}\cdot0.7\ \mathrm{Mpc}=35\,000\ \mathrm{pc}$, we see that the formal answer has no real sense. There is no real sense for the question about the angular size as well (formal answer is 130 radians).

**Answer:** «situation is impossible - ситуация невозможна».

problems.title: α5. Cluster.
problems.statement: Astronomers find a "star" which position in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram is about $8^{\mathrm m}$ higher than the corresponding stars of the main sequence. Assume that the "star" is a cluster of similar stars and estimate the number of stars in the cluster.

answer.note: The native solution explicitly rejects an exact 1585-star answer and preserves its printed magnitude-difference sign.

difficulty.rationale: Convert an approximate magnitude excess into a rounded equal-star population.

provenance.evidence: Complete personal visual reading of native question page 2 and native theory-sketch pages 5; estimated relative to stated prerequisites, no human calibration and no separate model checker.

solution.statement:
Let us consider that the absolute stellar magnitude and lightness of the cluster are $M(\text{cluster})$ and $I(\text{cluster})$, of a star in the cluster is $M(\text{star})$ and $I(\text{star})$. Initial relationship is:

$$I(\text{cluster})=I(\text{N-stars})=N\cdot I(\text{one-star}).$$

So

$$\lg I(\text{N-stars})=\lg N+\lg I(\text{one-star}),$$

$$\lg N=\lg I(\text{N-stars})-\lg I(\text{one-star}),$$

$$5/2\lg N=5/2\lg I(\text{N-stars})-5/2\lg I(\text{one-star})=\Delta M,$$

$$\lg N=2/5\Delta M,$$

$$N=10^{0.4\cdot\Delta M}.$$

As it done

$$\Delta M=M(\text{cluster})-M(\text{one-star})=M(\text{N-stars})-M(\text{one-star})=8^{\mathrm m}.$$

So

$$N=10^{0.4\cdot8}=10^{3.2}=1585\ \text{stars}\approx1600\ \text{stars}.$$

**Answer:** about 1600 stars.

Note: Answer "1585 stars" is not correct! There is data "about $8^{\mathrm m}$", so it is approximate value. For example, by varying this value only by only $0.1^{\mathrm m}$ we will get range of formal answers from 1445 to 1738, and by $0.5^{\mathrm m}$: from 1000 to 2512.

problems.title: α6. Earth transit.
problems.statement: At November 7, 2005, the Mars opposition will occur. During this event Mars will be situated at $0.47\ \mathrm{a.u.}$ from the Earth, being quite close to the ecliptic line ($27'$ south of it) as observed from the Earth. For this event the Martian Space Agency is planning the near-Mars space mission with astronauts onboard purposed to observe the Earth transit the centre of the solar disk. To diminish expenses the space mission will follow the optimal way – to observe the transit from the minimum possible distance from Mars. In what constellation will Mars be observed from the station in the middle of the Earth transit?

answer.value: near the South Ecliptic pole in the Doradus constellation, near to Large Magellanic Cloud.

difficulty.rationale: Infer the direction from the nearest station that can view a central Earth transit.

provenance.evidence: Complete personal visual reading of native question page 2 and native theory-sketch pages 6; estimated relative to stated prerequisites, no human calibration and no separate model checker.

solution.statement:
[[figure:p6-sol-fig1]]

While middle of the Earth transit being observed from the minimal possible distance from Mars, Mars will be situated near the South Ecliptic pole in the Doradus constellation, near to Large Magellanic Cloud.

problems.title: β4. Pole star.
problems.statement: It is known, that the altitude of the Pole star above the horizon is numerically equal to the geographic latitude of the place of observation, and the direction to it is the direction to North. However there are some errors in these rules. Find the maximum errors (in $^{\circ}$ and $'$) while using this way to find the latitude of the place ($\Delta\varphi$) and the direction to North ($\Delta\beta$). The observations are carried out in the observatory Xinglong (Синьлун) near Beijing. The declination of the Pole star is equal to $89^{\circ}10'$. The approximate latitude of Beijing is $\varphi=40^{\circ}$.

difficulty.rationale: Distinguish latitude error from azimuth error caused by the pole-star offset.

provenance.evidence: Complete personal visual reading of native question page 3 and native theory-sketch pages 5; estimated relative to stated prerequisites, no human calibration and no separate model checker.

solution.statement:
Для широты местности $\varphi$ эта погрешность $\Delta\varphi$ равна реальной разнице между высотами Северного полюса мира и Полярной звезды, которая может быть от $-\Delta\delta$ до $+\Delta\delta$, где $\Delta\delta=50'$ – разница склонений Полярной звезды и Северного полюса мира, то есть от $-50'$ до $+50'$. Таким образом, $\Delta\varphi=\Delta\delta=50'$.

Для направления на Север дело обстоит хитрее. Будем проводить на небесной сфере большие круги через точку Зенита и Полярную звезду в различные моменты времени. Погрешность определяется тем, как далеко от настоящего направления на Север упирается в горизонт конкретный большой круг. Максимальная погрешность $\Delta\beta$ – разница между большим кругом, проходящим через Северный полюс мира, и большим кругом, проходящим через Полярную звезду в её максимальном удалении по горизонтали. Для нахождения данной разницы спроектируем эти два больших круга на плоскость горизонта, получим две прямые, угол между которыми $\Delta\alpha$ находится из условия $\Delta\delta=\Delta\beta\cdot\cos\varphi$. Таким образом,

$$\Delta\beta=\Delta\delta/\cos\varphi.$$

Для широты Пекина:

$$\Delta\beta=\Delta\delta/\cos40^{\circ}=\Delta\delta/0{,}77\approx1^{\circ}05'.$$

problems.title: β5. Cluster.
problems.statement: Astronomers find a "star" of the spectral class A0 which position at the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram is about $-7^{\mathrm m}$ – $-8^{\mathrm m}$! (I.e. it is very much higher than the main sequence). Assume that the "star" is a cluster that consists of many similar stars and estimate the possible number of stars in the cluster.

answer.note: The native solution explicitly rejects exact endpoints 631 and 1585 and refers to α2 as printed.

difficulty.rationale: Estimate a population interval from spectral class and an approximate magnitude range.

provenance.evidence: Complete personal visual reading of native question page 3 and native theory-sketch pages 6; estimated relative to stated prerequisites, no human calibration and no separate model checker.

solution.statement:
Stars of A0 spectral class have absolute stellar magnitude about $0^{\mathrm m}$. So the problem is analogous to α2 with the difference in magnitude of "about $7^{\mathrm m}$ – $8^{\mathrm m}$". Analogous to α2 solution we can find approximate boundaries of number of stars in the claster.

$$N_{\min}=10^{0.4\cdot7}=10^{2.8}=631\ \text{stars}\approx600\ \text{stars}.$$

$$N_{\max}=10^{0.4\cdot8}=10^{3.2}=1585\ \text{stars}\approx1600\ \text{stars}.$$

**Answer:** about from 600 to 1600 stars.

Note once more: Answer about "from 631 to 1585 stars" is not correct! There is data "about $-7^{\mathrm m}$ – $-8^{\mathrm m}$", so we have approximate values.

problems.title: β6. Earth transit.
problems.statement: At November 7, 2005, the Mars opposition will occur. During this event Mars will be situated at $0.47\ \mathrm{a.u.}$ from the Earth, being quite close to the ecliptic line ($27'$ south of it) as observed from the Earth. For this event the Martian Space Agency is planning the near-Mars space mission with astronauts onboard purposed to observe the Earth transit on the solar disk (at least transit through the edge of the Sun) and to investigate the Earth's atmosphere. What minimum orbital period of motion around Mars must this space station have?

difficulty.rationale: Use transit geometry and a limiting eccentric orbit to obtain an orbital period.

provenance.evidence: Complete personal visual reading of native question page 3 and native theory-sketch pages 6; estimated relative to stated prerequisites, no human calibration and no separate model checker.

solution.statement:
[[figure:p9-sol-fig1]]

The angular radius of the Sun visible from the Earth is equal to

$$\rho=\arcsin(R/D)=16'.$$

Here $R$ is the radius of the Sun, $D$ is the distance between Sun and Earth. Let $L$ will be the distance between Earth and Mars. Being observed from the Earth, the angular distance between the Mars and ecliptic line $\gamma$ is larger than angular radius of the Sun, thus as can be seen in the figure, there will be no Earth transit on the solar disk observable from Mars, it will be a pity for Martians. To observe it anyway, they have to go by the distance $h$ towards the ecliptic plane (northwards). Taking into account that all angles are small and the Earth is many times smaller than the Sun, we will calculate this distance:

$$h=L\sin(\gamma-\rho)=0.0015\ \mathrm{a.u.}=224\,000\ \mathrm{km}.$$

To reach the distance required having the minimal orbital period, the Earth transit observation point must be the apocenter of the orbit. The pericenter distance cannot be less than the radius of Mars $r$ (about 3400 km). The minimal large semi-axis of the station orbit will be about

$$a=(r+h)/2=114\,000\ \mathrm{km}.$$

This value is 0.296 of the large semi-axis of the Moon orbit around the Earth. Calculating the period, we have to take into account that the mass of the Mars is 0.107 of the mass of the Earth. Using General III Kepler law:

$$a^3/(T^2M)=\mathrm{const},$$

we find that the station orbital period is about 0.49 of the lunar period or 13.5 days. For the mission to be successful, the station must be launched at October, 31, in three days after the theoretical round of X IAO.

The complete native task heading and two-line introductory caption are retained inside this direct rectangular crop because the tilted Sun circle overlaps the caption’s vertical range.

problems.title: αβ7. Рефракция.
problems.statement:
Зенитное расстояние ($Z$) определяется как угол между направлениями на астрономический объект и на зенит наблюдателя ($Z=0^{\circ}$ для объекта в зените и $Z=90^{\circ}$ для объекта на горизонте). Из-за атмосферной рефракции видимое (измеряемое) зенитное расстояние ($Z_m$) меньше, чем истинное ($Z_t$), на величину $R$ (в секундах дуги). Данные приведённой ниже таблицы могут быть использованы при наблюдениях на уровне моря при температуре $10^{\circ}$.

| $Z_m$ | R | $Z_m$ | R | $Z_m$ | R | $Z_m$ | R |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0° | 0″ | 50° | 70″ | 82° | 394″ | 87° | 863″ |
| 10° | 10″ | 60° | 101″ | 83° | 444″ | 88° | 1103″ |
| 20° | 21″ | 70° | 159″ | 84° | 509″ | 89° | 1481″ |
| 30° | 34″ | 80° | 319″ | 85° | 593″ | 89°31′ | 1760″ |
| 40° | 49″ | 81° | 353″ | 86° | 706″ | 90° | 2123″ |

Для зенитных расстояний $Z_m$ меньше, чем некоторое значение $Z_F$, приближённая формула для вычислений:

$$R=60{,}25''\cdot(B/760)\cdot(273^{\circ}/(273^{\circ}+t^{\circ}))\cdot\tan Z_m\qquad(1),$$

где $B$ – атмосферное давление в мм ртутного столба, $t^{\circ}$ – температура в °C.

parts.statement: Найдите диапазон значений $Z_m$, в котором можно использовать формулу (1) с точностью $1''$, т.е. найдите $Z_F$.

Найдите широту места наблюдения с точностью $0{,}1'$, если в то время, когда в июне Солнце наиболее высоко поднимается в небе, его наблюдаемое зенитное расстояние равно $16^{\circ}34{,}4'$. (Для заданной точности $\varepsilon=23^{\circ}26{,}4'$).
Вычислите (с точностью $0{,}1'$) истинное зенитное расстояние $Z_t$ для центра Солнца в тот момент, когда при заходе весь диск Солнца только что скрылся на горизонте ($t=10\,{}^{\circ}\mathrm C$).

Используя приведённую выше информацию, сделайте необходимые вычисления и нарисуйте видимую форму Солнца в тот момент, когда мы видим, что его нижний край только что коснулся горизонта. 1 клеточка в сетке соответствует $2'$. Пометьте, какие данные и метод вычислений Вы использовали при решении.

problems.statementAfterParts: Считать, что при отсутствии атмосферной рефракции угловой диаметр Солнца равен $32{,}0'$.

difficulty.rationale: Combine tabulated refraction, an approximation range and a solar-disk shape construction.

problems.title: β8. Планетарная туманность.
problems.statement:
Планетарная туманность – это расширяющаяся газообразная оболочка, образовавшаяся при взрыве центральной звезды. Шаровая планетарная туманность IC 418 наблюдается с помощью спектрографа, щель которого фиксирует лучи, пришедшие от точки примерно на половине радиуса туманности, как показано на рисунке 1. Рисунок 2 (по осям – поток и длина волны) – это полученная эмиссионная линия [N I], которая имеет лабораторную длину волны $\lambda=5200.26\ \mathring{\mathrm A}$. Явно видны два пика.

parts.statement:
**English**

Find Mars on the sky and show it.

**Русский**
